title: A left click on an aimed 1-HP zombie did not land when the world had been held (hitstop) for about a minute, through G, the Forge card, Esc and C; a hold begun at the zombie's staging landed it
evidence: CI run 40861397262 (fails, all three attempts) and run 40859622498 (passes, retry #2); frontend/tests/e2e/forge.spec.js@01816b14
note: Found writing W2-F step 5's e2e. The failing page showed the zombie's target frame at 1/100 and the Miner quest at 3/30: the two Buy clicks and the kill click each mined a block, since a headless page never holds pointer lock and opening the card leaves getInput().active true (a desktop browser loses the lock on G). Unverified hypotheses: something the click's verb routing reads (the melee cone or the aim cone) is refreshed only by a world tick, so a mob spawned under a long hold is not seen; or the routing read terrain nearer than the zombie. The spec now releases the walk's hold once the card is up and begins a fresh one at the staging (f10cc737). To close: stage the same kill under a hold begun 60 s earlier in a probe and read verbRouter's inputs at the click. UPDATE 2026-10-29 (d3545428): the same failure hit tests/e2e/talents.spec.js on all three attempts of run 40869763411 with no long hold (Stone 17, Miner 1/30, the zombie at 1/100), so the hold's length is not the variable. Both specs staged the zombie 2.5 m along the camera's facing on whatever floor stood there; the melee cone measures from the swing's apex over the body and drops a target past 4.5 m or more than 2.2 m above or below it (combat/cone.js), so the click fell through the verb router to the ground. tests/e2e/_meleeTarget.js now stages on the player's floor and requires GameMethods.checkMobsInMeleeCone to hold the zombie before the swing. Still unexplained: the TargetFrame showed the zombie while the click mined, i.e. the aim cone held it while the melee cone and the build ray chose otherwise. To close: confirm on CI that both specs pass first time over several runs, then close this row by that commit.

title: Until the next world step, a build ray passes through a cell placed since the last one, and through a chunk whose rebuilt trimesh took another chunk's broad-phase leaf
evidence: frontend/src/world/placedCellColliders.js (unindexed()), frontend/src/world/Terrain.jsx (castBuildRay, TargetOutline, the mob ground probes: world.castRay)
note: Rapier (rapier3d-compat 0.19.2) adds a collider to the broad phase only on a world step (measured 2026-10-30: a cuboid made between steps was missed by castRay and computeColliderMovement until the step). The player's sweep is cut against those colliders (game/kinematicMove.js); rays are not. So two clicks between one pair of frames aim the second through the first click's new cell, and when two chunks rebuild in one React commit their new trimeshes swap leaves and every ray misses them until the step. Not a path into the body. Fix direction: castBuildRay also casts against placedCells.unindexed() pairwise and takes the nearer hit. Raised from LOW on 2026-10-30, as the command session asked: the same window reaches the mob floor probe. mob-floor.spec.js:227 ('a roof over open ground') failed its first attempt on PR #59's certifying run 41073440534 (62159bc1, shard 5: 'under the roof, the floor is the ground', expected 52, received Infinity) and passed on retry #1. In the game a mob under fresh placements may read a wall for up to one step per rebuild. For the spec: its presence check no longer implies that the ground trimesh is indexed. The chaos-play gate now drives two clicks between one pair of frames a fifth of the time (about 170 pairs a file): no path into the body measured (I1 0 over 48 sessions). The ray itself still passes through the first click's new cell; that is this row.
